subject: FintechAI pricing follow-up: latency vs cost tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechai.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood pricing follow-up — recap + next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size pricing/architecture more precisely: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary use case: real-time transaction enrichment and explanation for customers at point-of-sale (low-latency inference on short prompts + few-shot context).
- Expected volumes: 50M–150M tokens/day initially, ramp to ~1B tokens/month within 12 months (rough estimate).
- Concurrency: bursty during peak hours — target 200 concurrent inferences at peak.
- Desired SLO: 99th-pct response time target between 200–500ms depending on route.

Open items for us to finalize pricing:
1) Confirm steady-state token mix (prompt vs completion ratio) and expected monthly tokens/month (range is fine).
2) Target $/1M tokens you have in mind (you mentioned wanting to be in the ~$20–$40 range if possible).
3) Which latency SLO is critical (200ms strict vs 500ms OK for some routes) — this changes tiering.

High-level next steps I propose:
- You share a short sample of typical prompts + avg output length (or a small telemetry export) — we can run a quick cost/latency sim.
- I’ll send a pricing summary (hosted tiers + dedicated committed pricing) and a one-page doc describing trade-offs (batching/streaming/quantization). Attached is a preliminary quote template.
- If it looks promising, technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Nikhil) to validate latency on a representative path.

Attached: Redwood-pricing-quote-FintechAI.pdf (draft)

If you can confirm the token range and whether 200ms is required end-to-end, I’ll prioritize the 200ms options in the quote.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Redwood pricing follow-up — recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: for budgeting purposes please assume a baseline of 600M tokens/month (this includes prompts + completions). We may ramp faster, but want to size conservatively.
- Target unit economics: we’re aiming for <$30 per 1M tokens for the long-term (committed) plan; for hosted/POC we can tolerate up to $50/1M.
- Latency SLO: core fraud-explain route needs ~200ms p99. Other enrichment routes can be 400–500ms.

Specific questions that impact pricing: 
1) How much does choosing Hosted Premium (lower latency) vs Dedicated (reserved capacity) change unit price at this volume?
2) You mentioned batching and streaming — can batching reduce cost materially for our profile? What trade-offs on p99 latency?
3) If we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity, what target $/1M tokens should we expect?

Procurement looped in for visibility — we’ll do an internal check on the compliance docs.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Product, FintechAI
sam.patel@fintechai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechai.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:05:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing follow-up — recap + next steps

Sam — great, thanks for the numbers. Below is a concise breakdown so you can compare apples-to-apples. I’ll attach an updated quote and SOW draft for procurement.

Quick unit-economics summary (estimates for your 600M tokens/month profile):

1) Hosted tiers (no infra commitment)
- Hosted Standard: ~$45 / 1M tokens — typical 99th-pct ~400–600ms (depends on prompt length). Good for POC and non-critical routes.
- Hosted Premium (latency-optimized, more expensive instance selection + priority routing): ~$70 / 1M tokens — typical 99th-pct ~150–250ms for short prompts (your fraud-explain path).

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — committed 12-month
- Dedicated Reserved: ~$18–$28 / 1M tokens (range depends on commit level + model selection). At your 600M/month baseline and a 12-month commit we’d expect toward the low end (~$20–$22/1M) after applying volume tiers and quantization recommendations.
- Note: Dedicated has an infra fee component (monthly GPU pool fee) and a consumption unit rate; we include both in the SOW.

3) How latency vs cost trade-offs work in practice
- Batch sizing: For high-throughput routes, batching can reduce per-token compute by 15–30% depending on variance. However, batching increases tail latency if you wait to fill batches — we use dynamic batching with latency caps to balance this. For your fraud route (200ms p99) we’d keep batch windows very small (lower cost wins are limited). For enrichment routes (400–500ms) batching gives more savings.
- Streaming: Streaming reduces time-to-first-token and looks better for perceived latency, but slightly increases token accounting for some models (marginal). It’s a good UX win for long outputs but less relevant for short real-time responses.
- SLO-driven pricing: For strict SLOs (200ms p99) we factor in higher instance classes, reserved capacity and higher routing priority which increases unit price. That’s why Hosted Premium vs Dedicated reserved costs diverge.

Suggested path for FintechAI:
1) Short-term POC: Hosted Premium for fraud-explain path (~$70/1M) + Hosted Standard for non-critical routes. This gets you low lift and a clear baseline.
2) Medium-term (60–90 days): Run perf tests, capture token telemetry and concurrency. If telemetry matches your 600M/mo profile, move to a Dedicated 12-month commit target ~$20–$25/1M for steady-state.

I attached an updated Redwood-pricing-quote-FintechAI.pdf and a draft SOW (SOW-draft-FintechAI.docx) with line items for Dedicated pool fees and a sample commitment schedule.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
- Share the updated quote and SOW (attached).
- Book a 60-minute tech deep-dive with Nikhil to validate p99 on a representative path (can do this Wed/Thu).

Can you confirm:
- That procurement has the SOW + quote and who the procurement contact is (if different from procurement@fintechai.com).
- Availability for the technical deep-dive (Nikhil’s calendar is open Wed/Thu afternoon PT).

Thanks — happy to adjust the numbers after we see telemetry.

Best,
Marissa
